title: The Chinatown band: Russ, Malep, Gordett and Joe Harris
summary: He lists his Chinatown band, how Pigeon arranged music, and how visitors sat in.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And also Henry Rust, we talked to Henry Rust a couple of weeks ago and he talked about when you played with him in Chinatown. Yeah, yeah, he too. Yeah, yeah. So who was in that band? It was just a four piece player?

Chinatown? Where? Chinatown? Chinatown? Raymond Carr was playing drums. See, Rust was playing drums first, then Rust switched to trumpet. You hired him on trumpet? No, he was, well, Gordette left me and went with Joe Robichaud, you understand, Robichaud's band. And Pigeon used to arrange music for me and Gordette was out there Chinatown. Used to arrange the music, you see. I used to get a lot of orchestration, big orchestration, well I'd swap for Walter, you know, for something small, or write something small for Riff, you know, with this outfit that I had. Well I had- You used to arrange too? Well I can write, but I never did have time. In fact I didn't take time, you understand what I mean? Because we, at that time, them guys, you had a band and you had to keep up with them because there was no addicts or nothing like that, but you were all drunks. Good drunks. Not Earl Malep. Earl Malep, yeah, he looked like a Mexican. Earl Malep was playing piano, he looked like a Mexican. Oh, and he's got some relatives that live out there. You're talking about the Chinatown? Yeah. Earl Malep was playing, I swung after- You were playing banjo then? Yeah, I was playing banjo at Chinatown. And Russ was playing drums? He was playing drums. And Raymond Carless, and I had Joe Harris on sax and then Russ was playing trumpet then. See I had Gordick was playing trumpet, but Sun Johnson and all them different musicians from all over the city used to come and sit in, you know, because we had a lot of music and the fellas would want to come where they could get their eyes open with that music. And of course we placed everything, out the latest of everything. Oh, they were learning the new tunes from you, the new notes. That's right, that's right. I helped them in there. Joe Harris, I had more trouble with him, trying to get him to learn how to read. He didn't want to read, he just wanted to rip all night, play like Handy, play like yourself, you understand me? And we see Handy and them was at the Black Gold, and Handy was around there, Smiley and Joe, Porter, and that bunch, and we closed them down. Oh yeah, we closed them down. You see, because we had a, you see, it wasn't integration then, but we had all colors to come up in that place, or where we was.
